name: sofia-sip
why: A SIP user-agent library opens a door into VoIP signalling, though as a library its surface is mostly plumbing.

brief.what_it_is: Sofia-SIP is an open-source SIP User-Agent library that implements the IETF RFC3261 signalling standard, meant to be built into client software for VoIP, instant messaging and similar real-time communication. An application hands it SIP and SDP traffic and gets back parsed, negotiated sessions it can use to set up media. The README does not name the programming language, but the build uses GNU autotools. The package also ships small command-line utilities (addrinfo, localinfo, sip-date, sip-dig, sip-options, stunc), which the README only partly describes.
brief.why_it_exists: The README presents it as a building block for SIP client software, so developers do not have to write a SIP stack from scratch. It is based on a SIP stack developed at the Nokia Research Center and is licensed under the LGPL.
brief.how_it_works: The library covers the SIP stack itself, including transports over TCP and UDP on IPv4 or IPv6 and signalling secured with SSL/TLS. A separate offer-answer module implements SDP negotiation per RFC3264, and STUN (RFC3489) lives in its own module so it can be used without the SIP stack. The README mentions only a few small utilities: sip-options queries a host with the SIP OPTIONS method, sip-date prints and parses SIP dates, addrinfo resolves host names, and localinfo prints local network interface information.

brief.install_notes: Build with GNU autotools: ./configure, make, make install. The README points to docs/devel_platform_notes.txt for compiling in other environments. The primary target is GNU/Linux. Homebrew's formula installs the executables listed above, but the README does not say anything about Homebrew, accounts, runtimes or first-run configuration. The README's source-control instructions refer to darcs and CVS, which look dated.
brief.standout: It is a complete RFC3261 user-agent stack with offer-answer negotiation and STUN, with the project copyright shared among contributors rather than dual-licensed. Its heritage is a Nokia Research Center stack, and FreeSWITCH carries it forward.
brief.status: Unmaintained upstream. The SourceForge homepage says 'This repository is not currently maintained.' and gives the latest release as 1.12.11 (2011-03-11). The same page says FreeSWITCH hosts a currently maintained version at github.com/freeswitch/sofia-sip, and that GitHub README is the one I read. I did not see a last-commit date on either page.
brief.caveats: The upstream project is not maintained, and the last release dates from March 2011. The primary target is GNU/Linux. It is a library, so it needs a client application built on top to be useful. The README does not document sip-dig or stunc, so their behaviour is unknown from these sources. The README's links to darcs and CVS repositories and to sofia-sip.org may be stale. The library is LGPL-licensed.
